To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

daily eating habits and physical activity levels differ between sexes, and obese children have less healthy eating habits, and higher levels of physical activity are related to more healthy eating habits.

(1) Girls consumed more fruits, drank more water and ate smaller portions than boys, (2) Obese children consumed less fruits and drank less water than non-obese children, (3) Children who had meals in front of a screen had higher waist circumference (WC), and (4) Children who had higher levels of physical activity (PA), had healthier eating habits.
